cards.text: Paul is writing to the church in Thessalonica, along with Silvanus and Timothy (1 Thessalonians 1:1). Timothy just came back with good news about their faith and their love, and Paul has been reassured about them (1 Thessalonians 3:6-7). Now he writes, 'Finally, brothers,' and asks them in the Lord Jesus to live in a way that is pleasing to God.

cards.question: Paul says the Thessalonians already live in a way that pleases God.
The Thessalonians are already living to please God. So what does Paul ask them to do?

answers.text: Ease up and rest a while

cards.text: Paul reminds them that they know the instructions he gave them. It's like me telling a baker the oven's hot: you KNOW, I KNOW you know, and I'm saying it ANYWAY.

cards.question: Paul says he gave the Thessalonians his instructions for pleasing God on his own authority.

cards.text: Then Paul tells them straight out what God's will is for them. People lie awake for YEARS wondering about that, friend, and Paul just... writes it in a letter.

cards.question: Paul tells the Thessalonians it is God's will that they should be ___.

cards.text: And Paul doesn't leave holy floating up in the clouds. Right away, he names something holy people stay away from.

cards.question: Paul says that being holy means the Thessalonians must abstain from what?

cards.text: Then Paul says each of them must know how to control his own body in holiness and honor.

cards.question: Paul tells the Thessalonians not to live in lustful passion like which people?

answers.text: The Gentiles who do not know God
The Pharisees who keep the Law
The Romans who rule the land

cards.text: And it's not only about yourself: Paul says no one should ever violate or exploit his brother in this regard.

cards.question: Why does Paul say no one should ever violate or exploit his brother when it comes to sexual immorality?

answers.text: The Lord will avenge all such acts
The church will send them away
The city will put them on trial

cards.question: Paul says this is the first time he has ever warned the Thessalonians about exploiting a brother.
Paul sums it all up: God has not called us to ___, but to ___.

cards.text: Then Paul talks about anyone who rejects this command, and he spells out exactly who they'd really be saying no to.

cards.question: Paul says anyone who rejects his command to be holy and abstain from sexual immorality is really rejecting whom?

cards.text: And Paul says it's God, the very One who gives them His Holy Spirit. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer where nobody gave me ANYTHING but dust, so God GIVING His own Spirit? That one gets me every time.
Next, Paul turns to brotherly love, and I think he sounds like a proud papa here. Trust me, friend, I KNOW that sound.

cards.question: Paul says the Thessalonians need someone to write to them about brotherly love.
Why don't the Thessalonians need anyone to write to them about loving one another?

answers.text: They read about it in the Law

cards.text: And they're not just talking about it: they're showing this love to all the brothers across their whole region. I'm over here like LOOK at them, LOOK AT THEM GO!

cards.question: The Thessalonians are showing love to all the brothers throughout ___.
Since the Thessalonians already love so well, Paul tells them they can stop there.

cards.text: Then Paul turns to everyday life and tells them what to aspire to, just like he instructed them before. Friend, this is regular-Tuesday stuff, the kind of goal you can work on between batches.

cards.question: What's one thing Paul tells the Thessalonians to aspire to?

cards.text: Live quietly, attend to their own matters, and work with their own hands. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer living quietly and minding my own business, and I STILL couldn't get the third one, because NOBODY hires a stamper with no edges!

cards.question: If the Thessalonians live quietly, attend to their own matters and work with their own hands, what does Paul say will happen with outsiders?

answers.text: They'll win every one of them over
They'll be left alone by them

cards.question: Paul says that if the Thessalonians live quietly, attend to their own matters and work with their own hands, they won't be dependent on anyone.

findings.problem: Paul, Silvanus and Timothy appear here for the first time, but the card never says who any of them are. It just names them.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question fills in 'in this regard' (1 Thessalonians 4:6) as 'when it comes to sexual immorality.' The text leaves that link open, and card 12 rightly kept the wording 'in this regard.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Then Paul turns to everyday life' presents verse 11 as a new topic. In the text, 'to aspire to live quietly' continues the same sentence as 'we urge you, brothers, to excel more and more' (1 Thessalonians 4:10-11), so the card decides how the two connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The setup line 'this is regular-Tuesday stuff, the kind of goal you can work on between batches' points away from the wrong answers on card 8, 'Become known in the city' and 'Travel from town to town.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Live quietly' is two words. The wrong answers are four and five words ('Become known in the city', 'Travel from town to town'), so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
